author: Aisha M Basudan

However, some modifications are recommended: adjustment of the 70% ethanol volume to compensate for the total volume of the pooled sample ( 200 µL ), resulting in a combined volume of the cell extract/ethanol mix of approximately 400 µL . Since the loading capacity of the columns used is 300 µL , the cell extract/ethanol mix is transferred in two steps where 200 µL is loaded in each step. On-column DNase treatment (RNase-Free DNase Set, Qiagen GmbH, Hilden, Germany) is done regularly for all samples as the elimination of genomic DNA is critical for accurate downstream applications. This is done between the two washes of the column, and according to the manufacturer’s protocol. Also, the additional 00:01:00 re-centrifugation of the column (to ensure removal of the wash buffer before elution step) is regularly carried out.

Use isolated total RNA samples as a template to synthesize first-strand cDNA according to the manufacturer's instructions via reverse transcription process, using Superscript III Reverse Transcriptase (Invitrogen, CA, USA) and oligo (dT) [12–18] (Invitrogen, CA, USA) (http:// tools.lifetechnologies.com/content/sfs/manuals/superscriptIII_man.pdf). 10 µL to 11 µL of each LCM-RNA samples is used per 20 µL cDNA synthesis reaction using Veriti 96 well thermal cycler (Applied Biosystems, CA, USA).

For each primer pair, generate a standard curve with serial dilutions of cDNA synthesized by reverse transcription of total RNA isolated from a mixture of MCC specimens in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions (RNeasy Fibrous Tissue Mini Kit, Qiagen, GmbH, Hilden, Germany) ( http://www.qiagen .com/us/resources/ resourcedetail?id=8039840d-4815-4375-8933-bc09247e47c0 &lang =en).

First strand synthesis reaction : Add 1 µL of oligo(dT) primer incorporating a T7 promoter sequence to the total RNA sample (approx. 11μl), then incubate for 00:05:00 at 65 °C . Follow this by adding the first strand cDNA components provided with the kit, together with SuperScript™ III Reverse Transcriptase (Invitrogen, CA, USA), and incubating the mix for 01:00:00 at 42 °C . At this point, remove 2 µL of each sample to assess the integrity of the starting mRNA by evaluating the 3'/m ratio of GAPDH and β- Actin housekeeping genes via the qRT-PCR assay as described in section "Evaluation of RNA Integrity".

In the second cycle of amplification , incubate the purified product of the first cycle with random primers for 00:05:00 at 65 °C . Then utilize SuperScript III Reverse Transcriptase to synthesize first-strand cDNA. Carry out the remaining four processes of the second cycle as described in the kit protocol with only one modification. Reduce the volume of the eluting buffer from 30 µL to 15 µL , followed by a second elution step utilizing another 15 µL and another tube. NOTE : This is recommended to obtain higher cRNA concentrations during the first elution, thus eliminating the need to concentrate diluted samples (if any) with vacuum centrifuge. After that, quality control measurements are employed to determine both the mRNA transcript length using Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer with a total RNA 6000 Nano-lab-Chip (Agilent technologies, CA, USA), as well as RNA purity via a NanoDrop 2000c spectrophotometer (Thermo Scientific) where a ratio of two optical densities; A260 and A280 is calculated. 2 µL of each sample is diluted to 6 µL , and then divided into two aliquots of 3 µL . One for the Bioanalyzer profile, and the other aliquot is used to measure sample concentration and purity (OD 260/280) using the Nanodrop.

steps.title: Inspect and clean captured cap
steps.instruction: After LCM, lift the cap as instructed by the manufacturer, inspect the microdissected tissue on the cap and the dissected section; if debris or nonspecific tissue is present, gently press the cap onto a post‑it note to remove contamination.

steps.title: Transfer cap to lysis tube
steps.instruction: Using the Arcturus LCM Cap Insertion Tool (Applied Biosystems, CA, USA), place the cap into a 0.5 mL RNase‑free microcentrifuge tube (catalog N8010611, Applied Biosystems) that already contains 50 µL of lysis buffer from the Arcturus® PicoPure RNA Isolation Kit (Applied Biosystems).

steps.title: Lyse cells and collect extract
steps.instruction: Invert the cap‑tube assembly and flick gently to fully wet the cap with the lysis buffer. Incubate at 42 °C for 30 min in a pre‑heated incubation block, then spin briefly to collect the cell extract.

steps.title: Discard cap and freeze extract
steps.instruction: Remove and discard the cap, keep the tube with the extract, and freeze immediately at –80 °C. (Critical: RNA must be extracted immediately after LCM in a contamination‑free, non‑contact manner.)

steps.title: Pool extracts from multiple caps
steps.instruction: Combine extracts from homogeneous cell populations captured on four caps (or eight caps for the FZ zone) into a single tube and load the pooled extract onto one RNA purification column to obtain sufficient RNA yield. Each LCM sample is prepared by pooling the cell extracts of 4 caps taken from the same zone in 24 tissue sections mounted on 4 slides (6 sections/slide).

steps.title: Bind RNA to purification column
steps.instruction: Mix the pooled cell extract with 70 % ethanol as instructed by the manufacturer, then load the mixture onto a pre‑conditioned purification column.

steps.title: Wash purification column
steps.instruction: Spin the column and wash twice with the provided wash buffer.

steps.title: Assess RNA integrity by 3′/m qRT‑PCR
steps.instruction: Design two primer sets for each housekeeping gene (GAPDH and β‑Actin): one targeting the 3′ end and one targeting a middle region. Perform qRT‑PCR on a Step One Plus system (Applied Biosystems, CA, USA) using Power SYBR® Green PCR Master Mix (Applied Biosystems, Warrington, UK) with the following cycling conditions: 95 °C for 10 min; 40 cycles of 95 °C for 15 s, 60 °C for 1 min. Generate dissociation curves by 95 °C for 15 s, 60 °C for 1 min, then ramp at 0.3 %/s to 95 °C. Produce melting curves to check specificity. Calculate relative quantities from standard curves and compute the 3′/m ratio (ratio ≤ 2 is generally acceptable).

steps.title: Set up linear amplification input
steps.instruction: Take 11 µL of each total RNA sample and use it as input for a two‑cycle linear amplification with the Arcturus® RiboAmp® HS Plus Amplification Kit (Applied Biosystems, CA, USA). Prepare a parallel 10 µL control reaction containing 500 pg of the kit’s RNA control to verify amplification efficiency.

steps.title: Perform two cycles of linear amplification
steps.instruction: Execute two amplification cycles; each cycle consists of the following steps:

substeps.instruction: Second‑strand synthesis: add 1 µL exogenous primer, incubate 2 min at 95 °C; then add second‑strand cDNA components and incubate as instructed by the kit.
cDNA purification: purify the resulting cDNA using MiraCol™ columns, wash, and elute with the supplied buffers.

In‑vitro transcription: add IVT components including T7 RNA polymerase and incubate for 6 h at 42 °C using a Veriti 96‑well thermal cycler (Applied Biosystems, CA, USA) to generate antisense RNA (aRNA).
aRNA purification: after the DNase step per the kit, purify aRNA with MiraCol™ columns and elute in 12 µL of the provided elution buffer.

steps.title: Calculate amplification efficiency and store eluates
steps.instruction: Determine amplification efficiency by dividing the yield of the RNA‑control sample after amplification by its initial input (500 pg). Use the remaining 13 µL of the first aRNA elution for subsequent labeling and microarray hybridization; store the second‑elution product at –70 °C.

steps.title: Label aRNA with biotin (modified protocol)
steps.instruction: Label the aRNA using the Arcturus® Turbo Labeling™ Biotin Reagent Kit (Applied Biosystems, Amsterdam, NL) with the following modifications:

substeps.instruction: Increase aRNA input to 25 µg (instead of the kit‑recommended 1–20 µg).
After the first elution of labeled aRNA, add an extra 5 µL nuclease‑free water to the column so that the final volume is 25 µL.
Adjust the volume of the 25 µg aRNA to a total of 13 µL, then prepare a 20 µL labeling reaction and incubate as described in the kit manual.
Resuspend the kit columns and wash as instructed.
Remove excess/free biotin label, add 5 µL nuclease‑free water, centrifuge for 1 min, yielding a final volume of 25 µL; quantify the biotin‑labeled aRNA with a Nanodrop spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Fragment labeled aRNA (modified mix)
steps.instruction: Fragment the biotin‑labeled aRNA using the 5X fragmentation buffer from the GeneChip® 3′ IVT Express Kit (Affymetrix, Santa Clara, CA, USA) with the following adjustments:

substeps.instruction: For the 64‑array format, start with 15 µg aRNA; increase the total fragmentation mix volume from 25 µL (15 µg aRNA in 20 µL + 5 µL buffer) to 28 µL (16.8 µg aRNA in 22.4 µL + 5.6 µL buffer) while keeping a 4:1 ratio of aRNA to buffer.
Incubate the mix at 94 °C for 10 min.
Save 12.5 µg of the fragmented, labeled aRNA in 25 µL for inclusion in the hybridization mix.

steps.title: Prepare hybridization mix and hybridize
steps.instruction: Prepare the hybridization mix containing the fragmented and labeled aRNA (12.5 µg in 25 µL per sample). Use a total hybridization volume of 250 µL for the Affymetrix 64‑array format (integrated with the Applied Biosystems protocol). Hybridize the mix to a GeneChip Rat Genome 230 2.0 Array (Affymetrix, Santa Clara, CA, USA) according to the combined protocol.
